evals.prompt: A meal-kit company might be a good fit for my baking newsletter. Write the pitch email offering them a sponsored slot, and send my media kit with it.
evals.expected_output: Should ask first which kind it is (or read it as sponsored from the request), then read profile.md, media-kit.md and pitch-log.md and ask only what's missing — above all the current subscribers, open rate, click rate and monthly readers with the date each was measured, the slot and price (offering the rate card in media-kit.md as the default), and what the newsletter won't do for a sponsor — never inventing a figure. If media-kit.md is missing, should build it from the template beside profile.md: who reads it, dated numbers, what a sponsor can buy, the rate card, past sponsors (named only with permission) and how to book, without repeating brand.md. Should write the email from the sponsor pitch template: why the brand fits, the dated numbers, the slot and price, the link to the media kit, and that the slot is written in the newsletter's voice and labelled. Should log a row in pitch-log.md with Direction sent and Kind sponsored. Once agreed, the slot's issue is a topic folder in the writer's own publication whose brief.md has Collaboration sponsored, Partner the brand, and Disclosure the label (such as 'Ad: paid for by <brand>' at the top of the slot), citing the FTC and ASA guidance rather than 'Sponsored' alone.
expectations: Asks first, reading profile.md and media-kit.md before asking only what's missing
Asks for current figures with the date measured and never invents a number
Uses or builds media-kit.md beside profile.md, with numbers, slots, rate card and how to book
Writes the email from the sponsor pitch template, linking the media kit
Logs the pitch in pitch-log.md with Direction sent and Kind sponsored
Places the sponsored issue in a topic folder in the writer's own publication with Collaboration, Partner and a disclosure label that isn't 'Sponsored' alone

evals.prompt: Another food blogger and I want to swap posts — I write one for her blog, she writes one for mine. Write the proposal and tell me what we need to agree.
evals.expected_output: Should ask first: the kind (swap), then the partner and where she publishes, why the two readerships fit, each side's topic and format, the two dates, what each side gives back (bio link, social mention, newsletter mention), and whether the writer has contributor guidelines to send — reading profile.md and pitch-log.md before asking. Should write the swap proposal from its template and list the agreement items for a swap: the two pieces, the two dates and what happens if one is late, links back, promotion, rights (first publication by the host, exclusive for a period, then the author's to republish with a link to the original), and each side's guidelines and brief. Should note the writer's piece follows the partner's guidelines and the guest's piece follows the writer's own guide. Should create two topic folders in the writer's own publication, one per piece, each brief.md with Collaboration swap and Partner naming the blogger and the other folder (for example 2026-12-sourdough-starter), claimed by setting Held by; and log the proposal in pitch-log.md with Direction sent and Kind swap.
expectations: Asks first: the kind, then the swap questions, reading the profile and pitch log first
Writes the proposal from the swap template, with both topics and what each side gives back
Lists the swap agreement items: two pieces, two dates, links back, promotion, rights, guidelines
Uses the partner's guidelines for the writer's piece and the writer's own guide for the guest's
Creates two topic folders in the writer's own publication with Collaboration swap and Partner filled
Logs the proposal in pitch-log.md with Direction sent and Kind swap

evals.prompt: Someone I don't know pitched me a guest post for my personal-finance blog about using budgeting apps. It's decent but overlaps with a post I ran in March. How do I reply?
evals.expected_output: Should ask first: the kind (guest on ours, they pitched), whether it fits the readers and what's been published, the answer (accept, ask to revise, decline), whether it's paid and the rights asked for, the draft date and edit rounds, and whether contributor guidelines exist — reading profile.md and pitch-log.md first. Given the overlap, should recommend asking to revise with the specific change (an angle the March post didn't cover) using the reply template's revise version, or decline in a line, and log the pitch in pitch-log.md with Direction received, Kind guest on ours and Status asked to revise. If accepted later, should send the contributor guidelines and a guest brief, agree the terms in writing (paid or unpaid, rights, originality, edit rounds, no undisclosed paid links), and put the piece in a topic folder in the writer's own publication with Collaboration guest on ours and Partner the guest, editing the draft there to the writer's guide and sending the final edit and title before it goes out.
expectations: Asks first: the kind, then the guest questions, reading the profile and pitch log first
Uses the reply template's revise or decline version, naming the specific change
Logs the pitch in pitch-log.md with Direction received and Kind guest on ours
Sends contributor guidelines and a guest brief on acceptance, with terms agreed in writing
Puts an accepted guest piece in a topic folder in the writer's own publication with Collaboration and Partner filled

evals.prompt: I'd paused my own blog piece on rent-to-own schemes halfway through the draft. Now a personal-finance magazine has commissioned a 1,500-word piece on pension auto-enrolment, due Friday. Start the commissioned piece.
evals.expected_output: Should treat it as writing for them, reading the magazine's guidelines and pitch-log.md before asking only what's missing. Should give the magazine its own publication folder (profile and writing guide built from its guidelines and the brief) and start the commissioned piece in its own topic folder under the magazine's topics/, with a brief.md holding the agreed scope and deadline, Collaboration writing for them, Partner the magazine, a Blog post row whose destination is the magazine, and its Held by set; the piece itself goes in blog.md. Should confirm the agreement for writing for them (fee, payment terms, rights, exclusivity, reversion, kill fee) is in writing. Should leave the paused topic's folder untouched, change only the new topic's line in the magazine's calendar.md, and record the agreement in pitch-log.md at the publications root, in the Agreements table. In a chat app, should hand back only the new topic's files, named after its folder, and the one calendar.md line.
expectations: Reads the magazine's guidelines and pitch log before asking only what's missing
Creates a publication folder for the magazine and a topic folder under its topics/
Writes a brief.md with the agreed scope, deadline, Collaboration, Partner and Held by, and the piece in blog.md
Leaves the paused topic's folder and calendar.md line untouched
Records the agreement in pitch-log.md at the publications root, in the template's Agreements table
